statement: For a holomorphically embedded pointed disc $(D,p)$ in a Riemann surface $Y$, choose a biholomorphism $f:\D\to D^\circ$ with $f(0)=p$. Its shadow is $df_0(\D)\subset T_pY$. In a local coordinate $z$ with $z(p)=0$, its radius is $r_z(D,p)=|(z\circ f)'(0)|$. Changing $f$ by a rotation changes neither the shadow nor its radius. Changing coordinate to $w$ multiplies the radius by $|dw/dz(p)|$.

statement: Fix any stable pointed complex curve $Y$ with at least one node. statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a connected stable graph of type $(g,n)$, with edge set $E\ne\varnothing$. Fix its pointed compact normalization components $X_v$, with every branch and external marking labelled. For an ordinary fibre, retain an identification of the normalization with these fixed objects; merely labelling the special points need not remove their finite automorphisms. All constructions below are equivariant for those automorphisms and also define the corresponding groupoid maps. We first take all external ends to be cusps. At each special point choose a local coordinate, used only to measure radii and tensor moduli. Let $I_v$ be the set of node branches on $X_v$. For $a\in[0,\infty)^E$, define $(B_va)_h=a_e$ when the branch $h$ belongs to the edge $e$; both branches of a loop are included separately. Let $H_v$ be the Jenkins--Strebel support function for these active points, with all other special points kept marked, and put \[ H_\Gamma(a)=\sum_v H_v(B_va),\qquad H_v(0)=0. \] Define the explicit open convex set \[ K_\Gamma=\left\{y\in\R^E: \sum_e a_e y_e<H_\Gamma(a) \text{ for every }a\geq0,\ \sum_ea_e=1\right\}. \] The attainable nonzero node tensors are exactly those with $(\log|q_e|)_e\in K_\Gamma$. Every such tensor system has a unique labelled geodesic-cut preimage, up to the equivalence of Theorem~\ref{A:fullcaps}. More precisely, if $x_e=(\ell_e/2\pi)^2$, the logarithmic modulus map is \[ G_\Gamma(x)=\sum_v B_v^T F_v(B_vx),\qquad G_\Gamma:(0,\infty)^E\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K_\Gamma, \] where $F_v$ is the vector of logarithmic cap radii on $X_v$. It is a real analytic diffeomorphism with symmetric positive definite derivative. In the phase coordinates specified by normalized cap maps, the complete tangent map is block diagonal with blocks $DG_\Gamma$ and the identity on $\R^E$. This is the tangent map on the fixed normalization fibre. When the normalization components also vary, the differential is block triangular with the identity on the normalization-moduli base and this invertible fibre block. In particular the full real tangent map is invertible everywhere on the fixed graph stratum.

statement: Let $(X,h)$ be a compact hyperbolic surface with geodesic boundary. Remove smooth open boundary collars so that the remaining surface $X'$ is diffeomorphic to $X$. Let $h'$ be its canonical hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary. There is a unique smooth real function $u$ on $X'$ such that $h'=e^{2u}h$, and it is characterized by \[ \Delta_hu=e^{2u}-1\quad\text{on }X',\qquad \partial_{n}u=-k_h\quad\text{on }\partial X'. \] Here $\Delta_h=\operatorname{div}_h\nabla$, $n$ is the outward unit normal, and $k_h$ is geodesic curvature measured toward the interior of $X'$. For collars cut at constant inward distance $a_i>0$ below their embedding widths, $k_h=-\tanh a_i$ on the corresponding new boundary and $u>0$ throughout $X'$. Thus $h'>h$ pointwise there.

statement: Let compact oriented bordered Riemann surfaces have finitely many paired boundary circles, and glue each pair by an orientation-reversing quasisymmetric homeomorphism, measured in analytic boundary coordinates. The topological quotient carries a conformal structure which restricts to the given structures on every interior, and its seams are quasicircles. It is unique under the identity on the pieces. More generally, for any given welding homeomorphisms, two realizations are conformally identical if one realization's seams are conformally removable. Rectifiable seams satisfy this uniqueness condition. Quasisymmetry is sufficient for existence and characterizes quasicircle realizations; it is not necessary for existence of arbitrary Jordan-curve weldings.

statement: Let $V$ be a Jordan disc and let $I$ be a Jordan arc with one endpoint on $\partial V$ and its remaining points in $V$. Cutting $V$ along $I$ gives a simply connected surface with a prime-end boundary circle. Its Riemann map has the boundary identifications of 67/071--073, with the slit tip and its two access points at the attachment prescribed as the three normalization points. No rectifiability is needed for this cutting assertion. Conversely, let the two designated boundary banks be identified by $\varphi$, and form their bank-exchanging involution $H$: $H=\varphi$ on one bank and $H=\varphi^{-1}$ on the other. Require $H$ to be quasisymmetric in an analytic boundary coordinate on the \emph{union} of the banks, including their common endpoint. This condition has a slit realization which is the image of a straight radial slit under a quasiconformal homeomorphism of a disc. After putting its tip at $0$ and its attachment at $1$ in the unit disc, the normalized realization is unique. Conversely every such quasiconformal slit pair has this welding condition. The correspondence is therefore with this specified class of slit pairs; quasisymmetry on a single bank alone is insufficient at the fold. For a prescribed rectifiable slit the normalized welding is unique, but ``rectifiable graph'' does not supply an existence criterion for an arbitrary interval homeomorphism.

statement: The interval homeomorphism $h(t)=t^2$ on $[0,1]$ is quasisymmetric, whereas the decreasing involution \[ H(x)=\begin{cases}-x^2&x\geq0,\\\sqrt{-x}&x\leq0\end{cases} \quad(-1\leq x\leq1) \] is not. For equal adjacent intervals at $0$, the ratio of the image lengths is $t^{1/2}/t^2=t^{-3/2}$, unbounded as $t\downarrow0$. To check the first assertion directly, for $t>0$ and $x\geq t$ the adjacent-increment ratio for $h$ is $(2x+t)/(2x-t)\in[1,3]$; the usual interval definition only tests triples in $[0,1]$. Thus the datum is quasisymmetric on one bank but cannot be the welding of a quasiconformal slit pair. We make no assertion here that it has no Jordan-slit realization in a larger class.

statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field with $\operatorname{char}k\ne2$, let $G=\operatorname{PGL}_2(k)$, and choose $i\in k$ with $i^2=-1$. The assignments $V'\mapsto N_G(V')$ and $\Gamma\mapsto$ its normal Klein four-subgroup give inverse bijections between Klein four-subgroups and subgroups isomorphic to $\mathfrak S_4$, in every characteristic different from~2. The assignment taking $V'$ to the union of the fixed points of its three nonidentity elements is a bijection onto the projective translates of $S$ if and only if $\operatorname{char}k\ne5$. statement: Let $(Y,D)$ be a stable pointed curve over a characteristic-zero field $K$. At a geometric node $e$, write $e^+,e^-$ for its two normalization branches and $L_e=T_{e^+}\widetilde Y\otimes T_{e^-}\widetilde Y$. A Galois-equivariant collection $N_e\in L_e\setminus\{0\}$ defines a stable log curve $Y_N^{\log}\to S_K^{\log}$, with thickness one at every node, and hence an outer action \[ \rho_N:G_K\longrightarrow\operatorname{Out}(\Delta_N),\qquad \Delta_N=\pi_1^{\log}(Y_N^{\log}/\overline S_K^{\log}). \] Here $\rho_N$ is the restriction along $s_t$ of the logarithmic base action. Its geometric group is the profinite fundamental group of a smooth surface of the same type as $(Y,D)$. Over $\mathbb C$ it is the profinite completion of the topological surface obtained by gluing the oriented real boundary circles at the nodes using the phases of $N_e$. The construction depends only on $(Y,D,N)$, not on higher order plumbing coordinates or a choice of smoothing family. After a finite extension splitting the nodes, take two tensor systems $N,N'$ on the same $Y$, and put $\delta_e=N'_e/N_e\in K^\times$. Identify their geometric groups and graphs by choosing compatible roots $\delta_e^{1/n}$ in $\overline K$. In the Dehn-twist coordinates of Hoshi and Mochizuki (2012), Theorem~4.8, the difference of the two outer actions is \begin{equation} \rho_{N'}(g)=T^{\kappa(\delta)(g)}\rho_N(g),\qquad \kappa(\delta_e)(g)= \bigl(g(\delta_e^{1/n})/\delta_e^{1/n}\bigr)_n \in\widehat{\mathbb Z}(1). \end{equation} The orientation of each twist is chosen to agree with the Kummer inertia of its smoothing coordinate.

statement: Take two labelled projective lines, each with node at $0$ and external marks at $1,\infty$, over $\mathbb Q$. Set $N=q\,\partial_z\otimes\partial_w$, $q\in\mathbb Q^\times$. statement: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $U/K$ be a geometrically connected hyperbolic polycurve: $U$ admits a finite tower of hyperbolic curves, in the sense of Mochizuki (1999), Definition~4.6. Let $(X_V,V)$ be its polystable compactification. \item Choose a connected finite \'etale Galois cover $W\to U$ dominating $V$, and normalize $X_V$ in $K(W)$, obtaining $Z$. \item Extend $G=\operatorname{Gal}(W/U)$ to $Z$ and set $\overline U=Z/G$. \end{enumerate} The resulting pair is independent, up to the unique isomorphism which is the identity on $U$, of all covers, towers, and field extensions in the procedure. The normal coarse boundary is not asserted to be log regular; the log-regular normalization $Z$ is retained whenever a log specialization theorem is applied.

statement: Let $K$ have characteristic zero and let $U/K$ be a smooth geometrically connected variety. Equivalently, the divisorial fine saturated log structure on $Z$ has trivial locus $W$ and is log regular. The existence of this cover is a property; no choice of it is part of the compactification data. \item For every excellent noetherian toric pair $(T,T^\circ)$ over $K$, every $K$-morphism $T^\circ\to U$ extends to a $K$-morphism $T\to Y$. \end{enumerate} When the interiors belong to an anabelian isomorphism category over $K$, meaning that their $K$-isomorphisms are recovered bijectively from their arithmetic fundamental groups with the $G_K$-augmentations, we call these its \emph{anabelian compactifications}. The interior and its embedding are retained; morphisms are morphisms of the pairs. Neither smoothness of $Y$ nor a log regular structure on its coarse boundary is imposed.

The two exact rows are \[ 1\longrightarrow F_2\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}_{0,4} \longrightarrow\mathfrak S_4\longrightarrow1, \] \[ 1\longrightarrow F_2\longrightarrow\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z) \longrightarrow\mathfrak S_3\longrightarrow1. \] The map between their finite quotients is $\mathfrak S_4\to\mathfrak S_4/V\simeq\mathfrak S_3$. In particular $\operatorname{PMod}_{0,4}$ is not $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)$.

statement: For every stable type $2g-2+n>0$, the profinite Teichm\"uller groupoids with the above tangential objects admit the natural $G_{\mathbb Q}$ action in pants/quilt coordinates. Fusing moves are controlled by the action on $\mathcal M_{0,4}$, simple moves by the elliptic moduli problem with a nonzero tangent vector, and local Dehn twists and half-twists by the cyclotomic character. The relations are the usual topological quilt relations, with changes of base object and stabilizers retained. At a fixed quilt this gives a lift to automorphisms of the profinite pure mapping class group; at each Galois element a different quilt changes that automorphism by a specified inner factor. The factor may depend on the Galois element: the assertion is equality of the outer actions, not conjugacy of the two entire representations by one fixed inner automorphism. The resulting outer action is compatible with inclusion of quilted subsurfaces and with filling boundary circles by marked discs.

statement: Let $U=\mathcal M_{0,4}=\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\setminus \{0,1,\infty\}$, choose the rational base point $2$, and set \[ \Delta=\pi_1(U_{\overline{\mathbb Q}},2)\simeq\widehat F_2. \] Fix an embedding $\overline{\mathbb Q}\hookrightarrow\mathbb C$, write $c$ for its complex conjugation, and let $H_c=\Delta\rtimes\langle c\rangle$, using the action supplied by the base point. This is the arithmetic fundamental group over the chosen real closure, and is the profinite completion of the corresponding extended pure four-point mapping class group. An element $\sigma\in G_{\mathbb Q}$ has its natural outer action on $\Delta$ induced by an automorphism of $H_c$ preserving $\Delta$ if and only if $\sigma\in\{1,c\}$. Thus the whole $G_{\mathbb Q}$ action cannot be extended to this single fixed real extended group with the indicated compatibility. There is instead a canonical outer action on the family $\{H_{\sigma c\sigma^{-1}}\}_{\sigma\in G_{\mathbb Q}}$ by isomorphisms between its members. With the chosen rational base point this action can be made strict inside $\Delta\rtimes G_{\mathbb Q}$.

statement: Every elliptic curve over $\mathbb R$, with its origin, is isomorphic over $\mathbb R$ to exactly one member of the following two disjoint families, with complex conjugation as real structure: \[ E_a(\mathbb C)=\mathbb C/(\mathbb Z+i\sqrt a\,\mathbb Z), \qquad E'_a(\mathbb C)=\mathbb C/ \bigl(\mathbb Z+\tfrac{1+i\sqrt a}{2}\mathbb Z\bigr), \qquad a>0. \] For a fixed complex elliptic curve admitting a real structure, there are two real forms. Except for the square lattice, they are either $\{E_a,E_{1/a}\}$ or $\{E'_a,E'_{1/a}\}$ with $a>1$. For the square lattice they are $E_1$ and $E'_1$. For the hexagonal lattice they are $E'_3$ and $E'_{1/3}$. The corresponding modular functions are \[ j(E_a)=j(i\sqrt a),\qquad j(E'_a)=j\bigl((1+i\sqrt a)/2\bigr). \] In each family $j(a)=j(1/a)$. In particular the guess $j=c\log a$ on 67/097 is false for every constant $c$.

statement: Fix a Weil cohomology theory and let $X$ be a smooth projective fourfold. Assume also that the primitive intersection form is positive semidefinite. Then numerical and homological equivalence agree in codimension two if and only if the primitive form is positive definite. In particular, the argument applies whenever the Lefschetz standard conjecture and the Hodge standard conjecture \emph{on homological algebraic classes} both hold. More explicitly, the \emph{class of applicability of the positivity argument} is the class $\mathscr C_H$ of polarized fourfolds with the displayed algebraic decomposition, nondegenerate divisor block and positive definite primitive block. Within the stated semidefinite setting, membership in $\mathscr C_H$ is necessary and sufficient for this argument to prove the comparison. This class includes all characteristic-zero fourfolds for Betti and $\ell$-adic cohomology, all abelian fourfolds using Theorem~\ref{B:abelian}, and smooth projective fourfolds admitting a finite surjective morphism from an abelian fourfold. This determines applicability of the argument; it is not a claim that varieties outside it fail standard conjecture~$D$. Independently of a positivity formulation, $\ell$-adic comparison in codimension two holds for every smooth projective fourfold $X$ admitting a dominant generically finite morphism $f:A\to X$ from an abelian fourfold, for every prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$.

statement: Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field $k$ and uniformizer $\pi$. In equal characteristic fix an isomorphism $R\simeq k[[t]]$ carrying $\pi$ to $t$. In mixed characteristic use the canonical Cohen inclusion $W(k)\hookrightarrow R$. Put $R_n=R/(\pi^n)$ and let $\mathcal R_n$ be its finite Greenberg ring scheme over $k$. For a $k$-algebra $A$, assume that $A$ is perfect in mixed characteristic, and define \[ S(A)=\varprojlim_n\mathcal R_n(A). \] For every $R$-scheme $X$, without a finite-type or separatedness assumption, the scheme \[ \operatorname{Gr}_R(X)= \varprojlim_n\operatorname{Gr}_{R_n}(X\times_R R_n) \] exists. There are natural bijections \[ \operatorname{Gr}_R(X)(A) \simeq\varprojlim_n X\bigl(\mathcal R_n(A)\bigr) \simeq X\bigl(S(A)\bigr), \] where all points on the right are morphisms over $R$. Here \[ S(A)\simeq \begin{cases} A[[t]],&R\simeq k[[t]],\\ R\otimes_{W(k)}W(A),&\operatorname{char}R=0,\ \operatorname{char}k>0. \end{cases} \] The construction preserves products and group objects. statement: Use standard $p$-typical Witt coordinates and write $[f]=(f,0,0,\ldots)$. For every commutative ring $A$, every $f\in A$, every $N\geq0$, and every $w=(w_i)_{i\geq0}\in W(A)$, one has \[ ([f]^Nw)_i=f^{Np^i}w_i. \tag{\(*\)} \] Consequently, for $A=\mathbb F_p[f]$, with $f$ an indeterminate, the canonical map \[ W(A)_{[f]}\longrightarrow W(A_f) \] is injective and is not surjective. An explicit element outside its image has coordinates $v_i=f^{-ip^i}$. The same conclusions and witness hold for the perfect domain $A=\mathbb F_p[f^{1/p^r}:r\geq0]$. In contrast, the vector with coordinates $w_i=f^{-i}$ does lie in $W(A)_{[f]}$. Thus this particular illustrative vector in \cite[Remark~18.3]{BBertapelleGonzalezAviles2022} must be replaced when using the standard-coordinate convention explicitly fixed in that source, Section~2.3, pp.~8--9. statement: Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, uniformizer $\pi$, and perfect residue field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Equal and mixed characteristic are both allowed. Fix a coefficient map $W(k)\to R$. For a finite product $L$ of perfect field extensions of $k$, put \[ R(L)=\varprojlim_n \bigl(W_n(L)\otimes_{W_n(k)}R/\mathfrak m_R^n\bigr), \qquad K(L)=R(L)[1/\pi]. \] For $R=k[[t]]$ with its specified coefficient field, these are $L[[t]]$ and $L((t))$. For $L$ a field, $R(L)$ is a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field $L$. Let $S_{\mathrm{pa}}$ be the étale site on finite products of perfect field extensions of $k$, $S_{\mathrm{pf}}$ the pro-fppf site on quasi-compact quasi-separated perfect $k$-schemes, and $S_{\mathrm{ir}}$ the pro-étale site on ind-rational $k$-algebras. Here rational algebras are finite products of perfections of finitely generated field extensions, and ind-rational algebras are filtered unions of rational subalgebras. In the pro-fppf site, coverings are finite jointly surjective families flat of profinite presentation in the perfect sense. The inclusions induce premorphisms \[ h:S_{\mathrm{pf}}\to S_{\mathrm{pa}},\qquad \widetilde h:S_{\mathrm{pf}}\to S_{\mathrm{ir}},\qquad \mathsf a=R\widetilde h_*Lh^*: D(S_{\mathrm{pa}},\mathbf{Ab})\to D(S_{\mathrm{ir}},\mathbf{Ab}). \] These premorphisms are not assumed to have exact inverse image on arbitrary sheaves of sets. \begin{enumerate} \item Let $\mathcal P'_{\mathrm{fc}}$ consist of commutative proalgebraic groups representable as extensions of perfections of abelian varieties by perfect affine groups, with finite étale component group. Restriction to $S_{\mathrm{pa}}$ is fully faithful on this category, and its derived counit is an isomorphism: \[ Lh^*(P|_{S_{\mathrm{pa}}})\simeq P \quad\text{in }D(S_{\mathrm{pf}},\mathbf{Ab}). \] \item The functors $R(-),K(-)$ induce premorphisms $\pi_R:R_{\mathrm{fppf}}\to S_{\mathrm{pa}}$ and $\pi_K:K_{\mathrm{fppf}}\to S_{\mathrm{pa}}$. Define \[ \mathcal R_R(F)=\mathsf aR\pi_{R,*}F,\qquad \mathcal R_K(F)=\mathsf aR\pi_{K,*}F,\qquad \mathcal R_x(F)= \operatorname{fib}\bigl(\mathcal R_R(F)\to\mathcal R_K(F|_K)\bigr). \] They give a functorial localization triangle. Call $Q\in D(S_{\mathrm{pa}},\mathbf{Ab})$ $h$-acyclic if its unit $Q\to Rh_*Lh^*Q$ is an isomorphism. If $R\pi_{R,*}F$ is $h$-acyclic, then \[ R\Gamma(L_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathcal R_R(F)) \simeq R\Gamma(R(L)_{\mathrm{fppf}},F). \] The analogous assertion holds over $K$. If both unit conditions hold for $F$ and $F|_K$, the analogous comparison holds with support on the closed fibre. Under this unit hypothesis, if both $F$ and $\mathcal R_R(F)$ are bounded below, there is the spectral sequence \[ E_2^{ij}= H^i(L_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathcal H^j\mathcal R_R(F)) \Longrightarrow H^{i+j}(R(L)_{\mathrm{fppf}},F). \] For algebraically closed $L$, this reduces to $\mathcal H^q\mathcal R_R(F)(L)=H^q(R(L)_{\mathrm{fppf}},F)$. \item If $G/R$ is a smooth commutative group scheme of finite type, write $G_n=G\times_RR/\mathfrak m_R^n$ and \[ \mathbf G=\varprojlim_n \bigl(\operatorname{Gr}_{R/\mathfrak m_R^n}(G_n)\bigr)^{\mathrm{perf}}. \] Then $\mathbf G\in\mathcal P'_{\mathrm{fc}}$ and \[ 0\longrightarrow U_G\longrightarrow\mathbf G \longrightarrow G_k^{\mathrm{perf}}\longrightarrow0 \] is exact, with $U_G$ connected pro-unipotent. Consequently $\pi_0(\mathbf G)=\pi_0(G_k)$, and $\mathcal R_R(G)\simeq\mathbf G[0]$. The unit condition in the preceding clause holds. \item If $N/R$ is finite flat and commutative, then $\mathcal H^0\mathcal R_R(N)$ is finite étale and agrees with $\mathcal H^0\mathcal R_K(N_K)$, $\mathcal H^1\mathcal R_R(N)$ is connected pro-unipotent, and $\mathcal H^q\mathcal R_R(N)=0$ for $q\geq2$. The object $R\pi_{R,*}N$ is $h$-acyclic. \end{enumerate}

statement: For a noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, the following three conditions are equivalent: $R$ is excellent and henselian; $R$ has the approximation property; and $R$ has the strong approximation property. Here approximation means that every solution in $\widehat R$ of a finite polynomial system over $R$ can be approximated to every finite order by a solution in $R$. Strong approximation means that, for each $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\in R[Y_1,\ldots,Y_N]^r$, there is a function $\beta:\mathbb N_{>0}\to\mathbb N_{>0}$ such that \[ f(a)\in(\mathfrak m^{\beta(n)})^r \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \exists b\in R^N:\ f(b)=0,\quad b-a\in(\mathfrak m^n)^N. \] In particular every complete noetherian local ring has strong approximation. The function need not admit a linear bound, even for $R=\mathbb Q[[s,t]]$.

statement: Let $k$ be a field. A higher stack here is a sheaf of spaces for the fpqc topology on affine $k$-schemes. An affine stack is $\operatorname{Spec}B$, where $B$ belongs to the homotopy theory of cosimplicial commutative $k$-algebras. For a pointed higher stack $(X,x)$ such that $k\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$, put \[ \mathbf U(X)=\operatorname{Spec}R\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X),\qquad \pi_i^{\mathrm U}(X,x)=\pi_i(\mathbf U(X),x)\quad(i\ge1). \] The derived algebra structure, including its cosimplicial commutative operations, is part of this definition. Then the following hold. \begin{enumerate} \item The map $X\to\mathbf U(X)$ is universal for maps to affine stacks. The stack $\mathbf U(X)$ is connected and hypercomplete, and its $\pi_i^{\mathrm U}$ are represented by unipotent affine group schemes, commutative for $i\ge2$. Here unipotent means that every nonzero finite-dimensional representation has a nonzero invariant vector. Finite type of these group schemes is not required. \item If $X$ is a scheme of finite type over $k$ and $x\in X(k)$, then $\pi_1^{\mathrm U}(X,x)$ is naturally the Tannaka group of the category of unipotent vector bundles on $X$, with fibre functor $x^*$. Here a unipotent vector bundle has a finite filtration by subbundles whose successive quotients are trivial line bundles. This is the unipotent Nori fundamental group in this specified sense. \item For every integer $r\ge1$, \[ H^j(X,\mathcal O_X)=0\ (1\le j\le r) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi_j^{\mathrm U}(X,x)=1\ (1\le j\le r). \] Under these equivalent conditions there are natural maps \[ H^{r+1}(X,\mathcal O_X) \simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_{r+1}^{\mathrm U}(X,x),\mathbf G_a), \qquad \operatorname{Ext}^1(\pi_{r+1}^{\mathrm U}(X,x),\mathbf G_a) \hookrightarrow H^{r+2}(X,\mathcal O_X). \] The extension group is for commutative fpqc group sheaves; the restriction $r\ge1$ ensures that its first argument is commutative. \item If $X$ is a proper $k$-scheme and $k$ has characteristic $p>0$, every $\pi_i^{\mathrm U}(X,x)$ is profinite. If moreover $k$ is algebraically closed, the comparison induced by $\mathbf F_p\to\mathcal O_X$ identifies its maximal pro-\'etale quotient with the affine group scheme associated to the pro-$p$-finite group \[ \pi_i\bigl(\operatorname{Et}(X)^{\wedge}_p,x\bigr). \] Here $\operatorname{Et}(X)^{\wedge}_p$ is the pro-$p$-finite completion of the entire \'etale homotopy type. The displayed group retains its profinite topology. Still assuming $k$ algebraically closed, if Frobenius acts bijectively on every $H^j(X,\mathcal O_X)$, these comparison maps are themselves isomorphisms. \end{enumerate} These conclusions concern a specified theory of schemes and higher stacks. They make no identification with the unspecified infinitesimal enrichment of the 1964 thesis sheet.

statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $n\geq2$, and let $X$ be a pointed higher stack for the fpqc topology on affine $k$-schemes. In particular, \[ \Phi_X^n\simeq (\pi_n^{\mathrm U}(X))^\vee, \qquad \mathbf M(\Phi_X^n) \simeq \varprojlim_r H^n_{\mathrm{Zar}}(X,W_r), \] where $W_r$ denotes the length-$r$ $p$-typical Witt-vector group and $\mathbf M$ is the formal-group Dieudonn\'e functor in the convention specified below. Smoothness, projectivity, ordinarity and finite formal-group height are not needed for this comparison.

statement: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated closed pair, degree-zero comparison for every \'etale sheaf of sets is equivalent to geometric henselianity. statement: For an arbitrary $\mathcal O$-module functor: \begin{enumerate} \item The map $u\mapsto\bar e_u$ from $E$ to formal additive-group actions has fibers exactly the additive cosets of $\ker\delta$. In particular the formal exponential map is bijective if and only if $\ker\delta=0$ and these three tests hold for every formal action. \item The map from globally nilpotent elements of $E$ to ordinary additive-group actions is always injective. Its image consists exactly of those actions for which there is one integer $r$ with $(\rho_R(\lambda)-1)^r=0$ for all $R,\lambda$, and whose logarithms satisfy \[ \log\rho_R(a\lambda)=a\log\rho_R(\lambda) \quad(a,\lambda\in R). \] It is bijective exactly when every ordinary action passes these two tests. \end{enumerate} These criteria distinguish failure of uniqueness, failure of unipotence, failure of scalar linearity, and failure to divide the formal parameter.
